T-ORDER.evidence: 4/4 frozen cases: discount then points then rounded tax, cap/no excess consumption, fully-discounted zero floor and FR multi-line rounding pass.

T-LOTS.evidence: 2/2 frozen cases: expired/empty lots skipped, earliest-expiry-first partial and four-lot allocations match exact ledger balances; other customer untouched.

T-IDEM.evidence: 6/6 frozen cases: original-result replay, changed-body rejection, foreign replay denial, tax-change stability and concurrent identical/mismatched keys all pass under a customer-level boundary.

T-RACE.evidence: 0/4 frozen cases fail at unchanged GET quote omitting points; supplemental all four yielding scenarios conserve all applied points, so this is not evidence of double spending.

T-REVERSAL.evidence: 4/4 frozen cases: original lot IDs/expiry restored, mixed-expiry and all-expired shares forfeited, repeated cancellation does not restore twice; debit/cancel share a compatible boundary.

T-AUTH.evidence: 3/3 frozen cases: missing session 401, foreign spend and foreign cancellation 403/404 with unchanged ledgers; replay is authorized and supplemental changed-owner replay rejects 404.

T-PENDING.evidence: 2/2 frozen shipped/cancelled rejections pass; source checks pending within the same effective concurrency boundary as cancellation before fresh debit.

T-CLOCK.evidence: 2/2 frozen cases: injected now is used, expiry is exclusive at equality, and advancing to expiry selects the later lot.

T-FAIL.evidence: 3/3 frozen pricing failures pass before saveLots; supplemental orders.save rejection after saveLots leaves [0,0,404], with no rollback of the debit.

T-EFF.evidence: 3/3 budgets pass: fresh records 8/8, next 7/7, replay 0/0, calls 3/3/1; private findAvailableByCustomer still scans/copies the global values list, so no indexed bound is established.

1. Order, conversion and rounding.why: T-ORDER 4/4: desired and applied quotes cap discounted cents, integer conversion is 1:1 and tax rounds after the point reduction.

2. Lots and clock.why: T-LOTS 2/2 and T-CLOCK 2/2: findAvailableByCustomer filters positive strictly-live lots at supplied time, sorts expiry-first and consumeEarliestLots debits partial lots.

3. Idempotency including mismatch.why: T-IDEM 6/6: order ownership is checked before replay; cloned original quote and requested points are stored on the order inside withCustomerLock across debit/publication.

4. Customer concurrency and failure atom.why: Store customer queue serializes full debit/cancellation and supplemental races conserve points, but saveLots commits before orders.save; supplemental publication rejection leaves the full 300-point debit stranded.

5. Reversal and expiry.why: T-REVERSAL 4/4: order allocations aggregate exact original lot IDs, getLotsByIds reads originals and only unexpired lots are restored once under the shared customer lock.

6. Authentication and ownership.why: T-AUTH 3/3 and supplemental changed-owner replay 404: authorization precedes cached quote, debit and cancellation restoration.

7. Pending-only eligibility.why: T-PENDING 2/2: pending is checked within withCustomerLock before fresh allocation; cancellation uses that same customer boundary.

8. Efficiency.why: T-EFF 3/3: fresh 8/8 records, next 7/7 and replay 0/0 with three/three/one calls; usable-only query and changed-lot writes work, but query still spreads/scans the entire private Map rather than maintaining an index.

9. Layering and pure domain.why: Routes adapt HTTP and application uses explicit ports/time, but allocation and reversal planning remain in application/redeem-points.ts and expiry ordering is in integration, not pure domain rules.

10. Final-report honesty.why: Public rerun confirms the report's nine existing tests; report accurately distinguishes a manual redeem/replay/cancel check and does not claim added tests, a real index or static checking.
